title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for diabetes and renal function.

HPI
The patient is a 54-year-old individual presenting for a scheduled follow-up regarding type 1 diabetes and established chronic kidney disease stage 4. The patient reports feeling stable overall. They have been managed on a long-term insulin regimen and do not utilize any oral medications for glucose management. The patient reports no acute changes in renal function or blood glucose levels since the last visit.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)

Exam
Patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination reveals no acute distress. Skin is intact without significant lesions. Renal function remains stable for current status.

Assessment
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus: Stable on current insulin therapy.
2. Chronic kidney disease stage 4: The patient’s renal decline is unrelated to diabetes.

Plan
Continue current insulin regimen. Monitor renal function labs every three months. Patient instructed to report any sudden changes in urinary output or edema. Follow up in three months.
explanations: The provider states the CKD is not due to diabetes: code each separately.
Code also the CKD stage (N18.4) as instructed at the diabetes CKD code or separately when unrelated.
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Provider documentation of no link overrides the presumption.
The stage of CKD must be reported with N18.-.
Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
